newsitem.title: FINLAND: Nokia bolsters Finnish shares as Europe tumbles.
newsitem.headline: Nokia bolsters Finnish shares as Europe tumbles.

text.p: Finnish shares outperformed weak European bourses but sagged to a lower close although underlying mood remained strong, brokers said.
The HEX index even rose briefly to a new life-high of 2463.8 right after the opening but it closed 0.12 percent lower at 2459.2 points. Turnover was a strong 503 million markka.

Bourse engine Nokia -- which had closed higher in New York on Tuesday than in Helsinki -- bolstered the market as other European bourses recoiled from recent high levels after the Dow Jones index tumbled overnight, they said.
Nokia closed up 1.30 at 262.50 markka, and trade was active at over 200 million markka.
"Shares could rise tomorrow as demand remained strong today despite the losses on Wall Street," said one. "This has been a quiet day, but the market has held up pretty well," said another.
Although bonds fell slightly, yields were still near historic lows and supported stocks, brokers added.
The forestry sub-index eased 0.71 percent, taking a breather in a rally since late last week. The largest forestry firm UPM-Kymmene lost 0.90 to close at 93.30 markka.
Metsa-Serla was flat after a few massive deals which made it the second liveliest stock of the session.
Mobile phone maker Benefon pared Tuesday's sharp losses on a profit-warning. It closed up 2.10 at 83.10 markka.
